samples.summary: Persisted CRDT schema widened: `list-item` nodes now keep a `headingLevel` attribute, and out-of-diff consumers of the shared tree were not considered
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.setBlockType` no longer pushes `headingLevel` onto `toRemove` when converting heading → list-item (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1413), so the attribute now survives on `list-item` nodes in the shared Yorkie tree. The backend reads it back unconditionally — `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:408-411` (`if ('headingLevel' in attrs) block.headingLevel = Number(...)`) — and `blockToAttrs` (docs-tree.ts:260) re-serialises it, so server-side reads/copies (`packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts`) now round-trip list items carrying heading levels. Any client build that predates this change still runs the old `toggleList`, which calls `setBlockType(id,'paragraph')` and therefore emits `removeStyleByPath(['headingLevel'])`, silently destroying the remembered level for every collaborator. Nothing in the diff versions or migrates the attribute.

samples.summary: Export/serialisation consumers were not updated for the new "bulleted heading" state, so the level is lost asymmetrically on every export path
samples.evidence: The new state (type `list-item` + `headingLevel`) is invisible to every exporter: `packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:111` emits a plain `- `/`1. ` item with no heading marker; `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:184` passes `block.type === 'heading' ? block.headingLevel : undefined`, so no `Heading N` pStyle is written; `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:201-202` filters `b.type === 'heading'`, so a bulleted heading is omitted from the PDF outline. DOCX import never produces list items at all (no `numPr` handling in packages/docs/src/import/*), so an export/import round trip downgrades the bulleted heading to a plain list item — the exact silent downgrade this change set out to fix, just moved to the export boundary.

samples.summary: Public `EditorAPI.getBlockType()` return shape widened — it can now report `headingLevel` together with `type: 'list-item'`
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2793 and packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1098 return `headingLevel: block.headingLevel` unconditionally, and packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:616 re-exposes the same shape. Consumers happen to gate on `type` today (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-style-options.ts:112 and :127, used by text-style-group.tsx:86/89), so nothing is broken right now, but the documented invariant "`headingLevel` implies heading" is now false across a package boundary and the interface docs on those signatures were not updated to say so.

samples.summary: The retention rule keys on `headingLevel !== undefined` rather than on the previous type, so a non-heading block carrying a stale level would be resurrected as a heading on un-bulleting
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:260 (`if (prevHeadingLevel !== undefined) block.headingLevel = prevHeadingLevel;`) and the mirrored guard at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1394-1395 do not check that the block was actually a heading. Any path that leaves a `headingLevel` on a paragraph/title/subtitle block would then turn into a heading on the next bullet-off. Paths that copy the field are pairs today (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:744, packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3404/3578/3607, clipboard parsing at packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:131) and `attrsToBlock` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:437) reads the attribute regardless of node type, so a legacy or remote node with a stale attribute would trip it. Gating on `block.type === 'heading'` would remove the dependence on that invariant.

samples.summary: `unlistedBlockType` is not exported from the docs package entry point, so out-of-package list toggles cannot share the helper the comment says keeps implementations from drifting
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:333-336 claims the helper keeps "the three `toggleList` implementations" in sync, but packages/docs/src/index.ts does not re-export it. Today every toggle either lives inside packages/docs (editor.ts:2870, text-box-editor.ts:1125, text-editor.ts:2169) or delegates to it (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:625-626, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:779/783), so nothing is broken — but a future frontend/slides-side toggle would have to re-hardcode `'paragraph'`.
